title: HALEU fuel supply for advanced reactors
bottleneck: Most advanced reactor designs need high-assay low-enriched uranium, HALEU at 5 to 20 percent U-235, yet no commercial HALEU supply exists. The only significant production is in Russia, and Western enrichment capacity is years from operation. The US has funded demonstration-scale enrichment, but output is measured in hundreds of kilograms against future demand of tonnes per reactor per year. Reactor startups cannot order fuel that does not exist.
why_it_blocks: HALEU is a single-point failure for the entire advanced reactor pipeline. Dozens of designs, billions in investment, and national deployment timelines all assume a fuel supply chain that has not been built.
current_state: The US DOE is standing up HALEU production and funding private enrichers, with the IRA investing 700 million dollars in a domestic supply chain. Commercial-scale Western HALEU remains several years away.
